AI VIDEO VISUAL PRODUCTION — SCENE BY SCENE
SCENE 1 — THE UNEXPECTED RESIGNATION
Dialogue — Founder:
"I quit! Two years of doing my marketing agency's job!"
Visual direction:
Open inside a premium Australian corporate office with a glass-walled meeting room, timber meeting table and professional executive setting.
A frustrated male business owner, approximately 42 years old, storms into the room carrying a cardboard box containing a laptop, marketing reports, notebooks and charging cables.
He drops the box heavily onto the meeting table.
The female HR manager looks up from her laptop, visibly startled.
The founder leans forward and delivers his line angrily.
Camera direction:
Start with a wide cinematic office shot.
Follow the founder entering the room.
Cut sharply to the box hitting the table.
Rapid push-in to the founder's angry face.
Acting direction: The founder should look exhausted, frustrated and completely serious.
Sound: Loud box impact followed by a short pause and subtle dramatic background music.
SCENE 2 — THE CONFUSING REVELATION
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"Sorry — you work for your agency?"
Dialogue — Founder:
"No! I pay them! My Google Ads spend keeps climbing, but revenue doesn't!"
Visual direction:
The HR manager sits upright in her chair, clearly confused by the statement.
She slowly lowers her reading glasses.
The founder immediately points towards himself, then drops printed advertising reports and invoices onto the table.
Show a brief, realistic close-up of a laptop displaying a fictional advertising performance dashboard. Advertising expenditure has increased while revenue remains largely flat.
The dashboard is illustrative and must not resemble an actual Traffic Radius client result.
The agency representative is visible sitting nervously at the far end of the meeting table.
Camera direction:
Tight close-up of the HR manager's confused expression.
Reverse close-up of the founder.
Brief dashboard insert.
Quick reaction shot of the agency representative.
Sound: Paper impacts and a restrained comedic pause.
SCENE 3 — THE RAPID-FIRE QUESTIONING
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"Who builds the growth strategy?"
Founder:
"Me."
HR Manager:
"Who plans the campaigns?"
Founder:
"Me!"
HR Manager:
"Who writes the creative briefs?"
Founder:
"Me! Midnight! Sundays!"
Visual direction:
The HR manager begins questioning the founder with the seriousness of a corporate investigator.
Use fast alternating close-ups between the two characters.
Each response becomes more intense.
Introduce three brief flashbacks:
Flashback A — Growth Strategy
The founder is alone in his office, studying advertising performance reports and preparing a growth strategy on his laptop.
Flashback B — Campaign Planning
The founder is sitting at his desk planning Google Ads campaigns, reviewing product images, campaign budgets and customer acquisition data.
Flashback C — Creative Briefs
The founder is at his kitchen table late at night. The room is dimly lit, with a laptop, unfinished coffee and scattered notebooks.
He looks exhausted while writing instructions for advertising creatives.
Return to the office for his final emotional response.
Camera direction:
Rapid close-up exchanges.
Quick flashback cuts.
Dramatic zoom for the final answer.
Maintain consistent character appearances between office and flashbacks.
Sound: Short percussive beats with each answer. Background music gradually becomes more intense.
SCENE 4 — THE AGENCY'S DEFENCE
Dialogue — Agency Representative:
"We manage his account."
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"Manage? He's running your entire marketing department!"
Visual direction:
Reveal the agency representative clearly for the first time.
He is a polished professional in a dark business suit, sitting comfortably with an open laptop.
He speaks confidently, attempting to defend the agency.
The HR manager turns towards him in disbelief.
She gestures towards the founder, who is now standing beside a pile of marketing documents.
The agency representative becomes uncomfortable and slightly loosens his tie.
Camera direction:
Medium shot of the agency representative.
Abrupt reverse close-up of the HR manager.
Reaction shot of the exhausted founder.
Sound: Music briefly pauses before the HR manager delivers her response.
SCENE 5 — THE EXPENSIVE REPORT
Dialogue — Agency Representative:
"We send monthly reports."
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"So he does the thinking, and you send a PDF?"
Dialogue — Founder:
"Exactly! And nobody can tell me what's actually working!"
Visual direction:
The agency representative confidently opens a glossy monthly advertising report on his laptop.
It contains charts, tables and generic advertising performance graphs.
The HR manager stares at the laptop with a completely unimpressed expression.
Cut to the founder holding several invoices while pointing towards the report.
Show a printer in the corner producing another long marketing report as a small visual comedy moment.
Camera direction:
Over-the-shoulder laptop shot.
Close-up of the unimpressed HR manager.
Medium shot of the frustrated founder.
Short insert of the printer.
Sound: Quiet printer whir and understated comedy music.
SCENE 6 — THE UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTH
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"That's not a growth partner. That's an expensive inbox."
Dialogue — Agency Representative:
"Bit harsh."
Visual direction:
The HR manager leans forward and looks directly at the agency representative.
She delivers the line calmly, without shouting.
The agency representative looks offended but cannot offer a convincing response.
The founder nods silently in agreement.
Camera direction:
Slow cinematic push-in on the HR manager.
Static close-up of the representative.
Quick reaction shot of the founder.
Sound: Background music briefly stops to emphasise the punchline.
SCENE 7 — THE HR MANAGER'S SECRET
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"Harsh? I run an online shop. I wrote my own Google Ads strategy last night!"
Dialogue — Founder:
"You too?"
Visual direction:
The HR manager suddenly loses her professional composure.
She removes her reading glasses and slams her personal notebook onto the table.
The notebook contains handwritten marketing plans for her own fictional online store.
Quick flashback:
Show the same HR manager sitting at home at night, wearing casual clothes, reviewing Google Ads campaign performance on her laptop.
She looks exhausted while working on advertising strategy.
Return to the HR office.
The founder stares at her in complete disbelief.
Camera direction:
Dramatic close-up of the HR manager.
Rapid cut to the home-office flashback.
Sudden zoom into the founder's stunned expression.
Sound: Dramatic, slightly exaggerated musical rise.
SCENE 8 — THE COMEDIC BREAKDOWN
Dialogue — HR Manager:
"Move over. I'm quitting with you!"
Visual direction:
The HR manager stands abruptly, removes her employee name badge and drops it onto the table.
She picks up the founder's cardboard box.
The founder looks at her in disbelief before breaking into a relieved smile.
Both characters storm out of the meeting room together carrying the box.
The agency representative remains alone at the table, still holding his monthly marketing report.
He slowly looks down at the report.
Then he looks directly towards the camera with an awkward expression.
The meeting room door swings shut.
Camera direction:
Wide shot as both characters stand.
Tracking shot following them towards the door.
Static shot of the agency representative sitting alone.
Final cinematic close-up of the door closing.
Sound: Comedic music reaches its peak, followed by an abrupt stop when the door closes.
SCENE 9 — THE TRAFFIC RADIUS REVEAL
Closing voiceover:
"Your business needs a growth partner, not another job. Traffic Radius. Book your free strategy call and find out what's holding back your growth."
Visual direction:
Hold on the closed meeting room door for a dramatic pause.
Transition to a polished, modern Australian digital marketing office.
Show quick cinematic shots of a professional marketing team reviewing Google Ads campaign performance, analysing conversion tracking, discussing creative ideas and mapping out an advertising strategy.
These shots should communicate an agency actively taking responsibility for strategy and execution.
Transition to a matte charcoal background with subtle Traffic Radius blue and green lighting accents.
Reveal the official Traffic Radius logo in the centre, preserving its original white rounded background and tagline exactly as supplied.
Keep the logo clearly visible while the closing voiceover plays.
Do not add any additional graphics, subtitles, headlines, CTA text or written messages within the video.
Sound:
Shift from the comedic soundtrack to a professional, uplifting instrumental background track at low volume.
The voiceover should sound confident, natural and distinctly Australian.
End with a clean musical resolution.
3. AI VIDEO GENERATION INSTRUCTIONS
Characters
Founder
Fictional Australian male, approximately 38–45.
Charcoal casual blazer and cream shirt.
Tired but professional appearance.
Expressive facial movements.
Natural Australian accent.
Maintain the same character identity across all scenes.
HR Manager
Fictional Australian female, approximately 38–45.
Charcoal business blazer, light blouse and reading glasses.
Professional and authoritative appearance.
Moves from confusion to disbelief and finally emotional frustration.
Natural Australian accent.
Agency Representative
Fictional Australian male, approximately 30–40.
Professional dark suit and tie.
Corporate, self-assured appearance.
Gradually becomes uncomfortable.
Natural Australian accent.
Cinematography
Ultra-realistic cinematic commercial style.
Authentic Australian corporate workplace environment.
Natural facial expressions and accurate lip-sync.
Realistic acting rather than exaggerated animation.
Rapid dialogue exchanges.
Dramatic facial close-ups.
Natural handheld camera movement where appropriate.
Consistent lighting, furniture and character positioning.
Realistic flashbacks maintaining each character's identity.
No cartoon effects, artificial-looking faces or unnecessary CGI.
Voiceover and audio
Preserve every dialogue line exactly as written.
Do not generate any extra character dialogue.
All spoken dialogue must use natural Australian accents.
Maintain consistent voices for all three characters.
The closing voiceover should be professional and motivational.
Keep cinematic background music at a lower volume than speech.
Use brief pauses to emphasise comedic moments.
Ensure all sound effects support the action without overwhelming dialogue.
 
Important production requirements
No added on-screen text, headlines, captions or subtitles.
No fake client success statistics.
No advertising platform logos.
Any performance dashboard must be clearly fictional and used only to illustrate the founder's situation.
Do not show Traffic Radius as the ineffective agency.
Reveal Traffic Radius only in the final branded scene.
No presenter delivering the advertisement directly to camera.
Ensure dialogue, character continuity and realistic acting take priority over elaborate visual effects.
Overall storytelling flow:
Frustration → Confusion → Questioning → Agency Excuses → Realisation → Unexpected Twist → Traffic Radius as the Growth Partner.
